chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibnarrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ali ibn Shajara, from one of the sons of Misam, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to pray facing the seventh pillar from those facing the doors of Kinda, and the distance between him and the seventh [pillar] was the measure of what a goat could pass through.

key_terms.أَبْوَابَ كِنْدَةَ: Doors of Kinda (a specific entrance to the mosque)
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Where did Imam Ali (AS) stand when praying in the Grand Mosque of Kufa?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the flexibility of the Qibla direction within the Grand Mosque of Kufa, noting that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) prayed facing the seventh pillar near the Kinda doors with a distance equivalent to a goat's passage. This detail underscores the scholarly understanding that the entire mosque structure served as a valid prayer space, allowing for slight variations in orientation without invalidating the prayer, a key point in Shia fiqh regarding the sanctity and utility of Al-Kufa.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ali Bin Shajara, from one of the sons of Misam who said,
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws used to pray Salāt by the seventh pillar from what follows the doors of Kinda, and between himasws and the seventh (pillar) was a measurement of what a goat could pass by from’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Ali ibn Shajarah from certain individuals of sons of Mitham who has said the following: “’
Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would perform Salah (prayer) toward the seventh pillar which is before al-Kindah door with a remaining distance of the size of a goat between him and that pillar.”
